body:
> Technically we could just do a regexp that extract a jsDoc comment then work from there, if it requires us to just add @name InstantSearch, that's ok I guess. There should not even be a need to entirely parse the JavaScript file.

There is some inference from the code: names and types.

> The parts we had to reformat (.bind(this)) are not used as for the documentation so I hope we can workaround this.

This is part of stage-2, and basically we have this preset only to support this syntax. Can we work with that and move forward? (the only file being impacted is InstantSearch.js).

We can also workaround that by using babel to process the files prior to using jsdoc-parse. Since this is only syntax sugar, that could work.

> If you only want to parse jsdoc comments (and not source code, as jsdoc does) then your best option is doctrine.

doctrine only works on extracted comments which adds yet another step...
